subject: EU residency vs US — unit econ and next steps for Avery Health
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@averyhealth.com>, procurement@averyhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quick residency & unit-econ qualifier (next steps)

Hi Sam / Avery procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the candid discussion on PHI scope and the residency constraints for your EU users. Short recap and a few asks so we can pull together a tailored pilot TCO: 

1) Token volume profile: could you confirm expected sustained monthly tokens and an expected 95th percentile tokens/day? On the call you mentioned "~2M/month" as a ballpark — helpful if you can confirm a more precise range (e.g., 1.5–2.5M).

2) Budget guardrails: what is the target unit-econ you're hoping to hit on a committed model? Customers often give a target in $/1M tokens (for us to size reserved capacity). If you have a range (e.g., $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens) that’s perfect.

3) Residency specifics: you flagged requiring EU-only data at rest and processing for certain workloads. Is that for all workloads or just the PHI subset? Also, do you have a preference for a specific cloud region/provider?

4) Timing & pilot: would a 3-month dedicated pilot with committed baseline make sense as the next step? We can surface an EU-backed reservation price and an equivalent US price for comparison.

Attached: redwood_pricing_sheet_q2.pdf — high-level price bands and the typical uplift for EU-residency + SOC2/HIPAA options. I also attached a token-estimate template for you to drop in actual call volumes.

If helpful, Marissa (Sales Engineer) can join a 20–30m follow-up next week to walk through the cost model and caching/quantization levers that materially change $/1M. Suggested times after 4/14 — what works for you?

Best,

Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Diego.Fernandez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0194

Attachment: redwood_pricing_sheet_q2.pdf (PDF, 312 KB)
Attachment: avery_token_estimate.xlsx (Excel, 14 KB)

From: Sam Park <sam.park@averyhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@averyhealth.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 16:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick residency & unit-econ qualifier (next steps)

Diego — thanks for the follow-up and the attach. Quick answers below to help your sizing: 

- Monthly token volumes: rough baseline 1.8M tokens/month across the product. Peak days (e.g., during batch analysis runs) can hit ~420k tokens/day (95th percentile ~200k/day).
- Profile: roughly 70% short prompts (<=128 tokens), 30% longer assists (avg ~600 tokens) for care summarization.
- Target unit econ: we’re sensitive to per-token cost. Leadership has given a soft budget target of $900–$1,100 per 1M tokens as the acceptable range for a committed pilot. Anything above ~1,200 will be hard for procurement to justify without very strong latency/throughput guarantees.
- Residency: the PHI workflows must be EU-only processing & storage. Non-PHI analytics can run in US if there’s material cost leverage.
- Preferred cloud region: we’d like Azure West Europe or GCP europe-west1 if possible.

I attached the token-estimate spreadsheet with our traffic slices filled in so you can run the unit-econ. Please also call out any incremental compliance / logging fees we should expect for EU residency.

Next steps: happy to do the 20–30m follow-up. I’m available Wed 4/15 09:00–11:00 CET or Thu 4/16 14:00–16:00 CET.

Thanks,
Sam Park
Product Lead — AI Integrations | Avery Health
sam.park@averyhealth.com | +44 20 7946 01 23

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@averyhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick residency & unit-econ qualifier (next steps)

Sam — really helpful, thanks for filling the sheet. A couple of concrete points and a recommended pilot structure below.

Quick pricing context (high level):
- Baseline hosted per-token price (US region, Q2 list) = $1,000 per 1M tokens (example band for the model profile you used).
- EU residency uplift = typically +10–15% versus US public region in our pricing bands (driven by EU region infra costs, additional logging/audit retention, and KMS/HSM integrations). For your profile I’d model a conservative +12% so EU baseline ~ $1,120 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated reserved capacity: with a 3–6 month committed baseline we can compress unit cost materially — expect 10–20% reduction vs hosted list depending on commitment size and burst profile. Given your 1.8M monthly baseline, a modest reservation would push the EU unit price closer to ~$950–$1,000 per 1M tokens.

Ways to improve effective $/1M quickly:
- Prefix/KV caching for common prompts — Marissa: we can show the 30% ordering pattern reduction in effective token count during the follow-up.
- Lower-precision quantization model variant for non-PHI analytics (run in US) — same API, lower cost.
- Batching and short-sequence optimizations on our runtime for summary flows.

Pilot recommendation (what I’ll put in the SOW draft):
- 3-month pilot, EU-residency for PHI flows on a dedicated reserved pool (Azure West Europe), committed baseline 1.5M tokens/month with 2:1 burst allowance.
- Offer: pilot EU committed unit price $1,050 per 1M tokens (includes SOC2/HIPAA logging + KMS integration).
- US fallback for non-PHI analytics at $900 per 1M tokens for the same period (can be mixed to optimize cost).
- Success criteria: 10%+ reduction in observed effective tokens via caching, and latency <200ms p50 for the assist flows.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Draft a short SOW + pricing addendum and send the DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.
2) Marissa will run a 20–30m session showing how caching/quantization impacts your model profile (she’s copied here).
3) If procurement is comfortable, we’ll prepare a short 3-month PO-friendly SOW that maps to the committed baseline pricing above.

Please confirm if Azure West Europe is acceptable for the EU residency requirement and which date/time you prefer for the Marissa session (Wed 4/15 09:00–11:00 CET / Thu 4/16 14:00–16:00 CET).

Thanks — we’ll make sure the SOW calls out the EU logging/retention terms explicitly.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Diego.Fernandez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0194

--
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
